To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the volatilisation rate of ammonia from poultry litter in aviary houses for layer hens was linear to the ammonia concentration in the water in litter and that the total ammoniacal-nitrogen concentration in the litter was linearly related to the pH, the temperature and the water content of the litter.
the emission of ammonia from aviary houses can be reduced by keeping the dry matter content of the litter at 90% or higher, and by maintaining a high temperature and a low pH in the litter.
the ammonia volatilization is controlled by the pH, temperature and water content of litter and by the degradation of the organic nitrogen in the litter.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the physical and chemical relationships of volatilization and degradation in aviary houses and the results can serve to improve the management of aviary houses for the benefit of animal welfare, environment and economy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the volatilizing of ammonia and the decomposition of organic nitrogen in litter from aviaries is influenced by the same parameters, which are pH, temperature and water content.
the ammonia emission from litter is a result of a combination of physical and chemical processes, which can be described by a mathematical model.
the ammonia emission from aviary houses can be minimized by maintaining a low water content in the litter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the volatilisation of ammonia from aviary houses can be reduced by a combination of measures, such as the use of litter with low water content and low pH.
ammonia emissions from aviary houses could be reduced by increasing the litter dry matter content and by adding a chemical additive that reduces the degradation rate of nitrogenous components.
the degradation of nitrogenous compounds in aviary litter and the volatilisation of ammonia are closely related.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dry matter content of the litter must be kept high, which will reduce the degradation of organic nitrogen and thereby the volatilisation of ammonia.
the NH3-N concentration in water in litter is a good predictor of the ammonia volatilization from litter in aviaries.
the dry matter content of the litter must be high enough to minimize the emission of ammonia from aviary houses.
